result.topic_en: This page continues Riemann's Latin prize essay on heat conduction (Commentatio). It covers the invariance of expression (II) and of the curvature-type quotient (III) under changes of variables, the criterion for two quadratic differential forms to be transformable into each other, and the start of a geometric interpretation as a line element in an n-dimensional space.

dentibus transmutari eam in expressionem

lege dependentem. At si quantitates $b$ sunt

cifrae aequales evadunt. Unde si $\Sigma b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$

Perinde patet, si expressio $(II)$ non evanescat,
expressionem

mutatis variabilibus independentibus non
mutari, insuperque immutatam manere
si in locos variationum $ds, \delta s$ expressiones
ipsarum quaelibet independentes $\alpha ds + \beta \delta s$,
$\gamma ds + \delta\, \delta s$ substituantur. Valores autem
maximi et minimi hujus functionis $III$ ipsarum
$ds, \delta s$ neque a forma expressionis $\Sigma b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$,
neque a valoribus variationum $ds, \delta s$ pendebunt,
unde ex his valoribus dignosci poterit, an
duae hujusmodi expressiones in se transformari
possint.

Disquisitiones haece interpretatione quadam
geometrica illustrari possunt, quae quanquam
conceptibus inusitatis utatur, tamen obiter
eam addigitavisse juvabit.

items.english: From the way this expression is formed it is evident that, when the independent variables are changed, it transforms into an expression that depends by the same law on the new form of $\Sigma b\, ds\, ds$.

items.quote:
Perinde patet, si expressio $(II)$ non evanescat,
expressionem
$(III)$ ... mutatis variabilibus independentibus non
mutari
items.english: Likewise it is evident that, if expression (II) does not vanish, expression (III) is unchanged when the independent variables are changed.

items.quote:
Valores autem
maximi et minimi hujus functionis $III$ ipsarum
$ds, \delta s$ neque a forma expressionis $\Sigma b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$,
neque a valoribus variationum $ds, \delta s$ pendebunt,
unde ex his valoribus dignosci poterit, an
duae hujusmodi expressiones in se transformari
possint.
items.english: The maximum and minimum values of this function III of ds, δs depend neither on the form of the expression Σ b ds ds nor on the values of the variations ds, δs. From these values one can therefore recognise whether two such expressions can be transformed into each other.

items.quote:
Disquisitiones haece interpretatione quadam
geometrica illustrari possunt, quae quanquam
conceptibus inusitatis utatur, tamen obiter
eam addigitavisse juvabit.
items.english: These investigations can be illustrated by a certain geometric interpretation. Although it uses unusual concepts, it will be useful to have pointed to it in passing.
